Docs/ Theme development/Block editor support

Block editor support

Tell the block editor about your theme: palette, alignments, supports, editor styles.

The block editor (Gotenberg) asks /wp-json/wp/v2/themes?status=active what the theme supports and styles its canvas accordingly. A theme package answers through theme.json.

Supports

"supports": {
  "title-tag": true,
  "post-thumbnails": true,
  "custom-logo": {"width": 240, "height": 80, "flex-width": true, "flex-height": true},
  "html5": ["search-form", "comment-form", "gallery", "caption", "style", "script"],
  "responsive-embeds": true,
  "align-wide": true,
  "wp-block-styles": true,
  "custom-spacing": true,
  "custom-line-height": true
}
Key Effect
title-tag the core prints <title>; always on in Pursae, kept for compatibility
post-thumbnails the Featured Image panel appears in the editor; .Thumbnail is filled for templates
custom-logo Site Identity gets a logo control with these dimensions; .CustomLogo renders it
html5 HTML5 markup for the listed parts (search form, comment form, galleries, captions)
responsive-embeds embeds get the wp-embed-responsive body class and the aspect-ratio CSS
align-wide Wide and Full alignments in the editor. Style .alignwide and .alignfull in your CSS
wp-block-styles load the opinionated core block styles (theme.min.css)
custom-spacing, custom-line-height padding/margin and line-height controls on blocks

Palette

"palette": [
  {"name": "Ink", "slug": "ink", "color": "#1d2327"},
  {"name": "Paper", "slug": "paper", "color": "#ffffff"},
  {"name": "Accent", "slug": "accent", "color": "#2271b1"}
]

The editor shows these colours in every colour control, and blocks that use them get has-<slug>-color / has-<slug>-background-color classes. The core prints --wp--preset--color--<slug> custom properties and the matching utility classes, so style your own elements with var(--wp--preset--color--accent).

Editor styles

editor_styles[] loads your stylesheet into the editor canvas (and TinyMCE in the Classic Editor). Keep typography, colours and content width there, and the editor matches the front end. Classic's assets/editor-style.css is a worked example.

Rendering blocks on the front end

Block markup is rendered by the core (the_content): static blocks come out as saved, dynamic blocks (latest posts, search, archives, categories, synced patterns, shortcode) are rendered in Go, and the block library stylesheet is always loaded. Your theme styles the result: .wp-block-* classes, .alignwide, .has-*-color, .wp-block-image figcaption, and so on.

Patterns and templates

Block patterns and the site editor's block templates are not part of theme packages in this version: /wp/v2/templates returns an empty list and the editor shows the core patterns only. Classic PHP-style templates (this section) are the way to build a theme.
